target_customer: Pharma and oncology patients treated through Asher's own clinical programs; commercially, biopharma partners and eventual payers for cancer and chronic infection immunotherapies
problem: Cytokines such as IL-2 activate many immune cell types at once, which causes toxicity and limits efficacy. Asher builds cis-targeted cytokines that act only on chosen cells such as CD8 T cells.
business_model: Venture-funded clinical-stage biotech; pipeline development with clinical collaboration and supply agreements, no product revenue
product_category: Biotech, cis-targeted immunotherapy (engineered IL-2 fusion proteins)

founders.name: Ivana Djuretic
founders.background_notes: MedCity News (2021-03) says she was a Pfizer colleague of Yeung; her education was not stated in the sources opened.

founders.name: Andy Yeung
founders.background_notes: Per MedCity News, he and Djuretic started Asher in 2019 after Pfizer relocated staff and they chose to stay in the Bay Area.

competitors.name: Synthorx
competitors.what: Engineered IL-2 candidate (THOR-707) for solid tumors
competitors.traction_then: Phase 1 stage; Sanofi agreed to buy it in December 2019

competitors.name: Nektar Therapeutics
competitors.what: PEGylated IL-2 (bempegaldesleukin) partnered with Bristol Myers Squibb
competitors.traction_then: Phase 3 development at the time of the Synthorx deal

technical_complexity.rationale: Engineering cis-targeted cytokine fusion proteins that bind two receptors on the same cell is research-grade protein engineering needing clinical development.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary protein engineering platform and patent filings (trademark filings from 2020), plus the long clinical and regulatory path that rivals must also walk.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals in IL-2 were acquired or struggled (Sanofi bought Synthorx in 2019; Nektar's drug later failed per Fierce), but no incumbent copied the cis-targeting approach in the sources found.

market_need_then: IL-2 was a validated but toxic cytokine; Sanofi paid about $2.5B for Synthorx in December 2019 and Merck later agreed to buy Pandion, which signals strong demand for better-targeted IL-2.

branding.name_origin: Per MedCity News (2021-03), Asher comes from Hebrew meaning blessed or fortunate, chosen to convey restoring health and happiness to patients (Yeung). A weaker directory source attributes it to Yiddish.

identity.voice_and_tone: Company site uses a light motif, for example the phrase light up a new path for immunotherapy

branding.brand_signature: Light up a new path (site tagline motif)

brand_strength.rationale: Low-profile science brand; coverage focuses on the science and financings, not the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Asher left YC in 2019 with a three-person team and raised a $55M Series A led by Third Rock in March 2021, a $108M Series B five months later and a $55M Series C in April 2024 with AstraZeneca and BMS joining. It is still active with a Phase 1b program and big-pharma combination deals announced in January 2025. Its success rests on a differentiated IL-2 platform in a market validated by Sanofi's Synthorx purchase, plus an experienced CEO hired in 2020. Clinical risk remains and no pivotal data are public.
notes: Series B lead: most outlets credit Wellington Management with participants as listed by FinSMEs; one aggregator says Third Rock led, treated as less reliable. The Business Wire page returned 403 so the Series B investor list comes from search snippets of FinSMEs and BioSpace. Synthorx and Nektar sources are dated 2019-12, about five months after the batch. Founder education not found. Series C date and investors taken from the BioSpace page.
